attempts.summary: Built an Ansible-driven WireGuard gateway topology on the Antrieb cluster: node2 serves an application on TCP 8080 bound only to a private LAN interface shared with node1 (10.10.20.0/24, the environment's egress:false "lan" network); node1 (VyOS) terminates a WireGuard tunnel (wg0, 10.10.30.0/24) for node3 and NAT-masquerades tunnel traffic onto the LAN so node2 sees requests as coming from node1. node3, which sits only on the shared mgmt network, can reach node2:8080 exclusively through the tunnel — direct attempts return connection failure, tunneled attempts return HTTP 200. All configuration was applied via a single Ansible playbook run from the designated control_node (node4), using SSH auth wired up with the cluster's shared keypair. All four managed nodes were then restarted one at a time via their native reboot mechanisms; boot-id changes were captured as proof of each restart, and full functional recovery (WireGuard handshake, NAT-forwarded HTTP access, blocked direct access) was reverified after every restart.
